chunks.content: ## Creating a Backlight Strip in Clover This section explains the step-by-step process of creating a backlight strip in Clover, including setting up name lines, preparing texture, and configuring material properties. 1. **Add a Name Line** Start by adding a name line where the backlight strip is required. Change the name line type to **text** to allow texture application. 2. **Prepare Backlight Strip Texture** Create the backlight strip text texture in Photoshop with dimensions **100x200 pixels** at a resolution of **300 dpi**. - Use either pre-existing textured images or scan actual material textures. - Process the texture image for optimal interface quality and save it. - Import this texture into Clover and apply it to the name line as the backlight strip texture. 3. **Set Backlight Strength and Material Properties** - Set the backlight strip strength to **20**. - Change the material setting of the backlight strip to **metal**. - Adjust the surface roughness to **40**. - Set backlight strength to **100** and metal density to **80**. 4. **Adjust Dimensions** - Set the thickness of the name line to **5 mm**. - Set the thickness of the actual backlight strip line to **1 cm**, which defines the width of the strip. --- ## Adding Backlight Strips to Curved Lines This section covers how to add backlight strips along curved paths using name lines, including troubleshooting texture issues and smoothing curves. 1. **Create Curved Name Lines** Use the free name line tool to add a circular or curved line where the backlight strip is needed. 2. **Adjust Name Line Attributes for Curves** The default settings for backlight strips are incompatible with curves, so: - Copy the existing name line in the canvas window. - Change the copied line to the original name line type. - Open the attribute editor and set: - Gap between name lines to **1.5 mm** - Length of each segment to **1 mm** - Thickness of the line initially to **0.30 mm**, then adjusted to **3 mm** 3. **Smooth the Curve and Remove Creases** - Use the **edit line tool** to select the line. - Open **curve and smooth** options in the attribute editor to eliminate creases in the texture, making the backlight strip appear smooth. - Use the **flip** function to reverse the direction of the backlight strip if needed. 4. **Fixing Edge Creases** - Small creases may appear at the ends of the lines on curves. - Add an additional line overlapping the crease and flip its direction to cover and smooth out the edge. 5. **Finalizing the Curve** - Continue adding new lines to the curve as needed, flipping direction to ensure smooth edges and consistent backlight strip appearance.
